An oxide of iron contains iron, its empirical formula, is :

(Given : Molar mass of Fe and O are 56 and respectively.)
en.explanation:
Let the oxide of iron contain 100 g of the compound.

Then,

Mass of Fe = 69.9 g

Mass of O = 100 − 69.9 = 30.1 g

Calculate moles of each element

Find the simplest whole-number ratio

Divide each by the smaller number (1.248):

This ratio is approximately 1 : 1.5.

To remove the fraction, multiply both by 2 :

In ,

Mass of Fe = g

Mass of O = g

Total mass = 160 g

Percentage of Fe = (approximately 69.9%)

Therefore, the empirical formula of the oxide is

Correct Option: B.

Fe का द्रव्यमान = g

O का द्रव्यमान = g

कुल द्रव्यमान = 160 g

Fe का प्रतिशत = (लगभग 69.9%)

इसलिए, ऑक्साइड का मूलानुपाती सूत्र है

सही विकल्प: B.
